Its, like, so hard to be able to pay them down because I'm unemployed and I've been on public assitanse for 6 months, its everything I can do to make my payments, so I think getting the equity from my house would be the best bet for me, unless you can structure a deal that takes into consideration the fact that my income is supplmementd publicly. nba_directive.reason_text: This client has expressed interest but cited a blocker (credit, income, or debt) — and with a nearly paid-down conventional mortgage at 3.99%, they are close to ready; a concrete removal plan for that specific blocker converts this slice at the highest rate.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by naming their blocker directly and reframing it as a solvable step, not a stop sign
  - Acknowledge exactly what they said is holding them back (credit score, income gap, or debt load)
  - Tell them: 'This is fixable — here's the specific path'

- Build a concrete blocker-removal plan tied to their actual situation
  - If credit: identify the exact score gap to qualification threshold, give 2-3 targeted actions (pay-down targets, dispute items, authorized user), and schedule a hard re-pull date on the calendar right now
  - If debt/DTI: calculate their current debt-to-income using the $477/mo P&I they already carry and identify which debts to eliminate or reduce to hit the qualifying ratio
  - If income: clarify what documentation gap exists and what timeline closes it (tax returns, YTD paystubs, offer letter, etc.)

- Anchor to their specific financial pain — do NOT pitch a cash-out refi off their 3.99% first mortgage
  - Their $81,572 remaining balance at 3.99% is a protected asset — make this explicit: 'We are not touching your first mortgage'
  - If consolidating debt is part of the picture, frame a HELOC or second lien as the tool — its rate, while higher than 3.99%, is a fraction of the 25-30% credit card rates they may be carrying
  - Reframe: 'Even at a higher HELOC rate, consolidating high-interest balances likely saves you real dollars every month — let's run your actual numbers together'

- Quantify the upside waiting on the other side of the blocker
  - Do not invent a savings figure — instead, tell them: 'Once we pull your updated credit/income picture, I can show you the exact monthly payment and total cost on the purchase you want'
  - Make the future state feel close and real, not abstract

- Lock in the next concrete step before ending the text exchange
  - Propose a specific action: 'Can we do a 10-minute call this week so I can map out your 60-90 day plan?'
  - Offer an alternative if they prefer async: 'Or I can send you a short checklist right now — which works better?'
  - Do not leave the thread open-ended; get a yes/no/reschedule, not silence
